$schema-note: Mutation ledger for the second channel runtime. Every row was APPLIED to the named file in the working tree, the named command was run from the repository root, the file was restored, and the recorded exit code is what that run returned. `killedCases` are read back out of the command's own output (none are parsed for node --test commands, whose failure lines vitest's pattern does not match; the exit code is the record there). Nothing here is a prediction.
tranche: M4.5 — packages/adapters/channel-discord, the second ChannelRuntime (founder decision D10: Discord first)
purpose: A green suite proves the code passes its own cases. Each row removes exactly one property this directory, its wiring or its configuration claims, and records whether a named case turned red.
procedure: node scripts/run-win271-mutations.mjs scripts/win271-discord-mutation-plan.json <results> — the same committed driver as the Slack sweep, now taking a plan path. Adapter rows run the adapter's vitest suites (which read the context through its built dist, unchanged by any row); composition rows run the composition-root audit, arch-boundaries, the generator's suite, or core-api's vitest suites over source.

commands.discordSig: pnpm --filter @platos/adapter-channel-discord exec vitest run src/discord-signature.test.ts src/rfc8032.test.ts
commands.coreApiConfig: pnpm --filter @platos/core-api exec vitest run src/config/sections.test.ts src/config/platform.test.ts

history: FIRST SWEEP (45 adapter rows): 44/45 killed. D32 'the global limit binds interaction followups' SURVIVED: the route carried a `globalBound` flag, and no case could tell it from its negation because a followup's rate-limit identity is a digest of the interaction token, never the bot token, so no bot's global block is ever looked up for it. The flag was dead logic and was DELETED from rate-limit.ts; the row was replaced by 'a global 429 is treated as an ordinary bucket 429', which is killed. Recorded rather than rewritten, because a survivor that removed code is the most useful thing a sweep finds.

The same first run also motivated three cases before it was counted: trailing garbage after a genuine signature and after a genuine key (Buffer.from hex truncation), and an unreadable 200 answer on a READ. Without them D08, D09 and D38 would have been equivalent mutants under node:crypto's own length checks.

VERIFIER ROUND 1 (head e974ac12) found three mutations the 52-row plan did not contain, each against behaviour this directory's own comments describe, and each SURVIVED the full suite: V3 a 429 naming no X-RateLimit-Bucket leaves its route free; V4 a thread-typed channel with no parent_id is keyed under an absent parent (`discord:undefined:<thread>`); V7 the rate-limit sweep deletes live windows. '52/52 killed' was true of the plan and overstated the suite. Round 2 added a case for each (discord-transport 33 -> 36 static cases, normalize 20 -> 21) and the three rows as D46, D47 and D48.

WRITING THE V7 CASE FOUND A LEAK. `bucketOfRoute` (route -> bucket) was never swept, and the sweep itself only ran once `resetAtByBucket` held 1024 windows. A followup's rate-limit identity is a digest of its interaction token, new for every slash command, so every followup whose answer named a bucket added one route entry for the life of the process. Measured on the e974ac12 build: 5000 followups on 5000 tokens -> bucketOfRoute 5000, resetAtByBucket 0, and no sweep ever ran. Round 2 counts all three tables towards the bound, records each window's (credential, bucket) group, drops a route entry once no window in its group is live (no `admit` answer changes: without a live window the route is admitted either way), and sweeps expired global blocks. Rows D49-D54 prove each half of that sweep can fail.
